title: Root Cause Analysis — Firewall Rule Error

fields.headline: Root Cause Confirmed: Self-Inflicted Outage
fields.narration: The root cause of the Retail VLAN outage has been confirmed. The firewall rule CM-2026-0087, created by IT Manager Jordan Kelley at 09:45, was intended to block inbound traffic from the 185.220.0.0/16 IP range. However, the rule was misconfigured: the source zone was set to 'any' instead of 'Untrust,' the source address was 'any' instead of 185.220.0.0/16, and it was positioned above the inter-VLAN allow rules. This meant it denied all traffic to the Retail VLAN — including from internal systems and authorized sources. No peer review was conducted, and no post-change verification was performed. The rule was deployed without validation. The system failed to catch the error because it lacked automated syntax checking, mandatory peer review for emergency changes, and post-implementation testing. This was not a cyberattack — it was a self-inflicted outage caused by a flawed change process.
keyFacts: Rule CM-2026-0087 was misconfigured: Source Zone = 'any', Source Address = 'any', Position = 3 above allow rules
No peer review or automated validation occurred on the emergency change
The rule was not tested after deployment
The Retail VLAN was isolated due to the rule's position and scope
The IT Manager acted under emergency policy but bypassed controls that would have caught the error
fields.expectedAction: The team must now conduct a post-incident review to identify systemic weaknesses in change management. Recommend immediate policy updates to require automated validation, peer review, and post-change verification for all emergency firewall changes.
fields.facilitatorNote: Read this inject aloud with deliberate pacing. Emphasize that the threat was real, but the response caused harm. The goal is not to assign blame, but to surface systemic failure points.
